title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Using a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and gpt-5-mini as the generator, we executed the preregistered paired confirmatory comparison under shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate reused across arms; at most one bounded repair allowed). All 240 pairs completed without infrastructure or model failures; every candidate passed the deterministic validator in both arms (n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0). The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Importantly, the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; that assumption does not hold for the executed shared-generation semantics and therefore the preregistered power plan does not apply to this run. We (1) present the preregistered design and artifact-backed execution accounting, (2) add an explicit statistical note explaining the degeneracy when discordant counts are zero, (3) document that a prespecified comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and point to the authoritative execution artifacts, and (4) outline reproducible next steps required to evaluate GVR’s operational value beyond this synthetic-verifier setting.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety concerns: stochastic generators can synthesize syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate invariants such as reachability, access-control lists, and workflow safety. Prior work therefore recommends interposing deterministic validators and generate–verify–repair (GVR) loops to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to ask the following research question: under a frozen, shared-generation design, does a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic-violation rates relative to a strong unconstrained baseline? Our contributions are: (i) a frozen preregistration and fully archived execution/analysis on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks); (ii) artifact-backed confirmatory statistics showing a null effect under the study’s shared-generation semantics; (iii) an explicit statistical clarification about the degeneracy of paired tests when discordant counts are zero; and (iv) a diagnostic reconciliation that explains how preregistered design choices (notably shared_initial_candidate) influenced sensitivity and interpretation, plus reproducible next steps.
sections.related_work: LLM hallucinations, fabrication, and unsafe generated code are well documented across domains and motivate validator-interposed architectures (surveys and systems reports summarized in the preregistration). Generate–Verify–Repair and constrained/grammar-guided decoding have improved mechanically checkable outcomes (e.g., compilation or executable syntax) in prior studies, and NetOps prototypes increasingly embed validators and human oversight to reduce operational risk. However, controlled, preregistered paired tests that specify generation semantics and compute paired estimands for semantic invariants are sparse. Our work builds on and complements prior methodological and systems literature by executing a preregistered paired confirmation focused on verifier-detectable semantic invariants rather than surface-level syntactic metrics.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration: The study (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) preregistered a paired estimand: the paired difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The public synthetic task bank comprised 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 tasks; each task encodes initial state, intent, workflow constraints, and expected final state. Generator and tools: requested generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Execution contract (frozen): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 (shared candidate reused across arms); maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded repair budget). Analysis plan: two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B) with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided; paired-bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Preregistration also specified conservative sensitivity analyses and contamination checks. The archived preregistration, execution manifest, and all analysis code/artifacts are authoritative for the design and outcomes.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate design produced one initial generation per task reused across arms; execution/model_configuration.json documents the requested model and stage counts; model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 240, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Confirmatory numbers from the registered analysis executor (analysis/results.json): baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair application: repair_applied = false for all episodes because the shared initial candidate satisfied verifier predicates in every task (representative scoring artifacts under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/). Missingness and exclusions: complete_pairs = 240; failed episodes = 0. Statistical note on degeneracy: when discordant cell counts n10 and n01 equal zero, the paired McNemar test is degenerate — there are no discordant outcomes to inform a directional or differential effect. In that case the exact McNemar two-sided p equals 1.00 and a nonparametric bootstrap of the paired difference yields a zero-width CI at 0.0; these values are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency and are correctly reported by the preregistered analysis executor (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/results.json). Interpretive consequence: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (randomized discordance potential); because the executed design used shared_initial_candidate semantics (documented in execution/model_configuration.json and deterministic_reconciliation.json), the preregistered power assumptions do not apply to this run. Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison: the preregistration listed two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B); the archived run executed only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing the unconstrained baseline (A) to the guarded GVR condition (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The execution artifacts (analysis/results.json and execution/model_configuration.json), and the deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) show that the schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed; no recorded rationale for that omission appears in the archived artifacts and we treat the omission as an unresolved procedural limitation.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and reconciliation: the null confirmatory result is artifact-grounded and expected under the archived semantics: reusing a single initial candidate per task meant the generator’s shared output already satisfied the verifier predicates for this synthetic task distribution and prompting, so the bounded repair stage never triggered. Two non-exclusive, artifact-backed explanations account for this outcome: (1) task/verifier alignment — the synthetic task distribution and verifier predicates produced a workload the generator (with the supplied prompt) could satisfy reliably; and (2) sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics — shared_initial_candidate removes per-arm stochastic variation that an independent-sampling design might expose and that GVR could exploit. Consequences for evaluation: a confirmatory null under these execution semantics is an informative empirical datum about redundancy of bounded GVR for these verifier predicates and generator/prompt pairing, but it is not evidence that GVR lacks value under independent-generation, adversarial, or cross-model conditions. Recommended reproducible follow-ups consistent with the preregistration and archived planned outputs: (i) rerun with independent per-condition generation (remove shared_initial_candidate) to restore discordance potential; (ii) inject adversarial/golden tasks designed to violate verifier predicates and measure repair utilization; (iii) evaluate multiple generator families and prompt variants; and (iv) integrate broader semantic/formal verifiers (e.g., SMT or constraint hybrids) to widen oracle coverage. Procedural limitation: the preregistered C vs B comparison was not executed and the artifacts record no rationale; this omission is reported transparently rather than post hoc explained.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment testing a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the preregistered shared-initial-candidate semantics, every initial candidate passed the deterministic verifier in both arms (n = 240 pairs), producing a null confirmatory result with paired estimate = 0.0, McNemar p = 1.00, and 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. The artifacts are authoritative for these numbers. The observed null demonstrates that (a) when a generator+prompting combination already satisfies a verifier’s encoded predicates on a task distribution, a bounded GVR loop will not reduce verifier-detected violations for those predicates, and (b) to evaluate GVR’s operational value more generally one must run independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model experiments and adopt stronger semantic or formal verifiers to measure residual risks outside the current oracle. We release the archived artifacts so others can reproduce the accounting and extend the evaluation under alternative generation semantics and adversarial conditions.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
